paper.title: Dominate or Delete: Decentralized Competing Bandits in Serial Dictatorship

settings.name_in_paper: Decentralized serial dictatorship (competing bandits in matching markets)
unmapped: N agents, K >= N arms; two-sided matching market with arms having uniform known preference (ranking) over agents
asymmetric collisions: arm matches only the highest ranked proposing agent, others blocked (reward 0, notified)
heterogeneous agent-specific arm means, all distinct per agent
regret per agent measured against the unique stable matching partner
decentralized: each agent uses only its own observations, agents know N (used in protocol)
settings.definition_quote: We consider $N$ agents, and $K\geq N$ arms. ... An agent is \emph{matched} to the arm of its choice in a given round, if and only if it is the highest ranked agent playing that arm at that time. Otherwise, it is \emph{blocked}. ... The regret of any agent $j \in [N]$, after $T$ time steps is ${R}_T^{(j)} = \sum_{t=1}^T  \mathbb{E} [\mu_{jk^{(j)}_*} - \mu_{j I^{(j)}(t)} \mathbf{1}_{{M_{I^{(j)}(t)}(t)} = j}].$

settings.name_in_paper: Decentralized serial dictatorship, Optimally Stable Bandits (lower bound)
unmapped: N agents, K >= N arms, serial dictatorship matching with asymmetric collisions
OSB instances: each agent's stable match partner is its overall optimal arm
regret per agent against stable matching
settings.definition_quote: Let us consider the class of bandit instances where dominated arms are bad, i.e. for any instance $\boldsymbol{\nu}$ in this class, for all agents $j \in [N]$,  $\mu_{jk} < \mu_{jk_*^{(j)}}$ for all arms $k \in [K]\setminus \{k^{(j)}_*\}$ . We call this class of instances Optimally Stable Bandits (OSB)

symbols.Coll_j: sum_{j'<j} sum_{k in A*_j} (9 alpha log T/(Delta^{(j')}_k)^2 + 1 + 178 T^{-4alpha}/(Delta^{(j')}_k)^2 + T^{2-4alpha}) mu_{j k*_j}  (collision regret)
symbols.Sub_j: sum_{k in A*_j minus k*_j} (9 alpha log T/(Delta^{(j)}_k)^2 + 1 + 178 T^{-4alpha}/(Delta^{(j)}_k)^2 + T^{2-4alpha}) Delta^{(j)}_k  (suboptimal pull regret)
symbols.i_star: min{ i in N : 20 N K alpha i / Delta^2 <= 2^{i-1} }, Delta = smallest gap of non-dominated arms across all agents

conditions: arm means in (0,1) and distinct for each agent

source.label: thm:main_thm_algo
source.quote: Suppose every agent runs \name\; with $\alpha \geq 2$, then the regret of any agent with rank $j$ satisfies \mathbb{E}[R_T^{(j)}] \leq 2(j-1)(\log_2(T)+1) + ... +N + j(2^{i^*}+i^* + 4(NK)^2 + 3NK) + \frac{2NK}{T^{2\alpha-4}}, where $i^* {:=} \min \left\{ i {\in} \mathbb{N}: \tfrac{20 NK \alpha i }{\Delta^2} \leq 2^{i-1} \right\}.$

results.notes: Per-agent regret against the stable matching partner (comparator mapped to best_policy as the closest; it's the stable-matching benchmark). Regret defined via means so pseudo_regret. Complex sums encoded via declared symbols. Algorithm does not need T or gaps.

symbols.Delta: smallest gap of non-dominated arms across all agents (min_j min_k Delta^{(j)}_k)

conditions: arm means distinct for each agent

source.label: cor:UBcor
source.quote: Suppose every agent runs \name\; with parameter $\alpha \geq  2$, then the regret of any agent with rank $j$ after $T$ time steps satisfies \mathbb{E}[R_T^{(j)}] \leq 9\alpha \log(T) \left(  \tfrac{(j-1)(K+1-j)}{\Delta^2} + \tfrac{[K-1-j]_{+}}{\Delta}\right) + O \left( (NK)^2 + \tfrac{NK}{\Delta^2}\log \left(\tfrac{NK}{\Delta^2} \right) \right)

results.notes: Leading term has explicit constant; additive term is O(.). Recorded with notation O overall. Proposition 4 (epsilon-Nash incentive property) not recorded as a regret bound.

symbols.LB_coll_j: sum_{j'<j} Delta^{(j)}_min / D_inf(nu_{j' k*_j}, mu_{j' k*_{j'}}, P)
symbols.LB_sub_j: sum over arms k of Delta^{(j)}_k / D_inf(nu_{jk}, mu_{j k*_j}, P)

conditions: OSB instance (stable match partner is each agent's optimal arm)

source.label: thm:lower_bound

results.notes: Uniformly consistent: system regret o(T^a) for all a on all instances. D_inf is K_inf-type quantity for agent pairs; encoded via declared symbols.

symbols.Delta: gap parameter of the constructed instance (smallest gap)

conditions: exists an OSB instance with Bernoulli rewards

source.label: corr:simple
source.quote: There exists a OSB bandit instance with Bernoulli rewards, where the regert of agent $j$ is lower bounded as $\Omega\left(\max\left\{\tfrac{(j-1)\log T}{\Delta^2}, \tfrac{K\log T}{\Delta}\right\}\right)$.

results.notes: Derived from Theorem 7 for uniformly consistent policies; proof gives (j-1)log(T)/(16 Delta^2). Asymptotic in T.
